This vignette describes how to add an adult mosquito (**MY**) model module to
[`ramp.library`](https://github.com/dd-harp/ramp.library). Before creating a
new module, check whether the model family is already available in the
SimBA library. For an overview of the component interfaces, see the
[`ramp.xds` MY interface vignette](https://dd-harp.github.io/ramp.xds/articles/MY-interface.html).

An MY module represents adult mosquito ecology and, when applicable, pathogen
infection dynamics in mosquitoes. It supplies methods that integrate with
[`ramp.xds`](https://github.com/dd-harp/ramp.xds), which provides the shared
model setup, transmission, egg-laying, and solver interfaces.

## Create a module template

This vignette's R code chunks can be extracted to create a starting R file.
Download `MY-How_To_Add_Model.Rmd`, set your working directory to the folder
containing it, then run:

```{r, eval=FALSE, purl=FALSE}
knitr::purl(
  "MY-How_To_Add_Model.Rmd",
  output = "adult-MY-newMYname.R",
  documentation = 0,
  quiet = TRUE
)
```

Replace `newMYname` throughout the extracted file with a short, unique class
name for the model. Review every placeholder and adapt the methods to the
model's equations and state variables before using the file.

## Conventions

- MY methods dispatch on the class of `xds_obj$MY_obj[[s]]`; use `s` as the
  vector-species index in method signatures and calls.
- Use `get_MY_vars(y, xds_obj, s)` to retrieve named state variables, and keep
  the order of variables consistent across `setup_MY_ix`, `get_MY_vars`,
  initial values, and the dynamics.
- Document the model's state variables, parameters, equations, assumptions,
  and relevant references in roxygen.
- Add tests for setup, parameter and initial-value changes, dynamics, and any
  model-specific outputs.

### Documentation policy

Follow the shared [function order](https://dd-harp.github.io/ramp.xds/articles/XH-interface.html#function-order)
in module files and guide implementation sections. Move functions with their
documentation, keep file-level review/TODO notes at the top, and preserve
definitions and behavior when reordering.

Follow the shared [documentation conventions](https://dd-harp.github.io/ramp.xds/articles/XH-interface.html#documentation-conventions)
and the [MY setup wording](https://dd-harp.github.io/ramp.xds/articles/MY-interface.html#setup-documentation).
These vignettes are the public style reference for both packages.

- Use the approved family titles with the module name in backticks and the
  **MY** tag. Bionomics titles are "Mosquito bionomics for `module`
  (**MY**)"; effect-size titles are "Apply effect sizes for `module`
  (**MY**)".
- Describe the actual equations, including accessory derivatives and
  delayed branches. Replace placeholder descriptions with formulas when
  implementing the model; keep returned states and equations in the same order.
- Keep storage, class assignments, and dispatch mechanics in `@note`.
  Describe generic dispatch on the generic rather than repeating it on methods.
- List setup actions in code order, including the constructor with
  `nPatches` and `options`, initial values, and any shared ports.
  End with "Return the updated **`xds`** model object."
- Use method-specific helper links for circadian and dispersal
  initialization, qualified with `ramp.xds::`, and end complete bullets
  with periods. Only list interfaces the method actually sets up.
- Describe skill sets as capabilities and compatibilities returned on demand
  by `get_skillset_MY`; do not store them on the module object. Explicitly
  include `dts = FALSE` when no discrete-time update method is defined.
- Document any checks actually performed. A no-op check returns the model
  unchanged; it does not validate the setup.

The minimal setup example below does not configure shared bionomics,
circadian, or matrix ports. Add the helpers required by the implemented
equations and document each call using the MY setup wording. Do not copy
matrix-port configuration without checking the module's needs.

## Module overview

```{r, eval=TRUE, purl=TRUE}
#' @title The `newMYname` module for the **MY** component
#' @section State Variables:
#' Describe the module's actual states and any derived quantities used by
#' its initial-density accessors.
#' @section Parameters:
#' Describe the parameters used by the implemented model, including their
#' biological meanings and units. Include `f`, `q`, `g`, and `sigma` if the
#' corresponding dynamical parameter accessors are implemented.
#' @section Dynamical Terms:
#' Describe the shared terms used by the implemented equations.
#' @section ODE:
#' Describe the continuous-time equations if the module implements `dMYdt`.
#' @section DTS:
#' Describe the updating equations if the module implements `Update_MYt`.
#' @section Egg Laying:
#' Describe the daily number of eggs laid per patch as the module's egg-laying
#' population times oviposition rate and eggs per batch.
#' [F_eggs.newMYname] returns this quantity before distribution among aquatic
#' habitats by [ramp.xds::EggLaying].
#' @name newMYname
NULL
```

## Dynamics

Implement one dynamics method for the model family: `dMYdt.newMYname` for a
continuous-time model, or `Update_MYt.newMYname` for a discrete-time model.
Both methods receive `t`, the dependent-variable vector `y`, `xds_obj`, and
the vector-species index `s`. Return values in the same order used for the
state indices.

Begin derivative descriptions "Compute the derivatives for the `module` module:"
and show the implemented equations immediately below, including accessory
derivatives and delayed branches. Inherit the module NULL anchor's relevant
sections. Document returned block order in `@note`, including matrix flattening
when applicable. Keep dispatch documentation on the shared generic.

```{r, eval=TRUE, purl=TRUE}
#' @title Compute the derivatives for `newMYname` (**MY**)
#' @description Compute the derivatives for the `newMYname` module:
#' Replace this placeholder with the equations for `dM` and `dY`,
#' in returned-vector order, when replacing the placeholder code below.
#' @inheritParams ramp.xds::dMYdt
#' @note Derivatives are returned in blocks for `M`, then `Y`, each in patch order.
#' @return a [numeric] vector of derivatives in the module's state-variable order
#' @export
dMYdt.newMYname <- function(t, y, xds_obj, s) {
  # Retrieve the shared terms needed by this model.
  Lambda <- xds_obj$terms$Lambda[[s]]
  kappa <- xds_obj$terms$kappa[[s]]

  with(get_MY_vars(y, xds_obj, s), {
    with(xds_obj$MY_obj[[s]], {
      # Replace these placeholders with the model's equations.
      dM <- ...
      dY <- ...
      c(dM, dY)
    })
  })
}
```

For discrete-time models, implement the update equations directly and return
the updated state vector; do not return derivatives or add them to the
current state unless that is the model's defined update rule.
Use "Update states for `module` (**MY**)" for the title and
"Update the state variables for the `module` module:" for the description,
followed by the updating equations in `\deqn{}`. Inherit the same NULL-anchor
sections as the derivative method, with `DTS` in place of `ODE` (or the
continuous-time `Dynamics` section). Document the actual return shape;
the existing RMdts and SEI list-return discrepancies remain deferred.

```{r, eval=TRUE, purl=TRUE}
#' @title Update states for `newMYname` (**MY**)
#' @description Update the state variables for the `newMYname` module:
#' \deqn{\begin{array}{rl}
#' M_t &= \ldots \\\\
#' Y_t &= \ldots
#' \end{array}}
#' Replace these placeholders with the implemented updating equations.
#' @inheritSection newMYname State Variables
#' @inheritSection newMYname Dynamical Terms
#' @inheritSection newMYname Parameters
#' @inheritSection newMYname DTS
#' @inheritParams ramp.xds::Update_MYt
#' @return a numeric vector of updated states
#' @export
Update_MYt.newMYname <- function(t, y, xds_obj, s) {
  with(get_MY_vars(y, xds_obj, s), {
    with(xds_obj$MY_obj[[s]], {
      M_next <- ...
      Y_next <- ...
      c(M_next, Y_next)
    })
  })
}
```

## State-variable extraction

`get_MY_vars.newMYname` maps the dependent-variable vector `y` to the named
state variables used in the equations. Include only variables that belong to
the module's state vector; do not add host variables unless they are actual MY
states.

```{r, eval=TRUE, purl=TRUE}
#' @title Get the state variables for `newMYname` (**MY**)
#' @description Extract the state variables for the `newMYname` module
#' from `y` and return them by name in a list for use during model solving.
#' @note Variable indices are stored at `xds_obj$MY_obj[[s]]$ix`.
#' @inheritParams ramp.xds::get_MY_vars
#' @return a named [list] of state variables and module-specific derived quantities
#' @export
get_MY_vars.newMYname <- function(y, xds_obj, s) {
  with(xds_obj$MY_obj[[s]]$ix, {
    list(
      M = y[M_ix],
      Y = y[Y_ix]
    )
  })
}
```

## Bionomics and effect sizes

For bionomic parameters managed
through shared ports, implement `MBionomics.newMYname` to evaluate their
baseline values at time `t`, and `MEffectSizes.newMYname` to apply the
intervention effects. These methods receive `t`, `y`, `xds_obj`, and `s`, and
return the updated `xds_obj`.

For each parameter `x` configured as a port, bionomics stores `x_t` and
resets `es_x` to 1; effect sizes set `x = x_t * es_x`. Parameters without
ports are stored directly as `x` and are not modified by effect sizes.
This also applies to EIP (`eip_t`, `es_eip`) and the standard dispersal
matrix (`K_matrix_t`, `es_K_matrix`). Matrix effects use elementwise `*`
and must preserve the dispersal-matrix constraints. Recompute demographic
and survival matrices using the realized parameters, and have dynamical
parameter accessors such as `get_f` read those values without applying
effects again. Document separately whether `get_MY_pars` reports baselines
or realized values.

The SI module is an example of a module using the shared parameter helpers
for feeding rate (`f`), human fraction (`q`), mortality (`g`), emigration
(`sigma`), emigration loss (`mu`), oviposition rate (`nu`), and EIP duration.
Use only the parameters relevant to the model.

## Interface outputs

Implement the following methods with one value per patch:

- `F_fqZ.newMYname` returns the daily density of infectious mosquito bites on
  humans (`fqZ`). The transmission interface uses it to compute EIR by human
  stratum.
- `F_fqM.newMYname` returns the daily density of mosquito bites on humans
  (`fqM`). The transmission interface uses it to compute HBR by human
  stratum.
- `F_eggs.newMYname` returns daily egg production by adult mosquitoes in each
  patch. The egg-laying interface distributes the eggs among habitats.

Each method receives `t`, `y`, `xds_obj`, and `s`.

For egg production, use "Compute egg production for `module` (**MY**)".
Use the description "Return the number of eggs laid by the adult mosquito
population, per patch" and return "a [numeric] vector of length `nPatches`".
Inherit the module NULL anchor's `Egg Laying` section using
`@inheritSection newMYname Egg Laying`. In that section, explain which
mosquitoes lay eggs: total adult density or, in behavioral-state
models, gravid density. Multiply that density by the oviposition rate and
eggs per batch. Link the method to its module and `ramp.xds::EggLaying`.

For biting outputs, describe daily biting density on humans in each patch,
not a per-host biting rate. Use the titles and numeric-vector return contract
below, link the two methods reciprocally, and explain any model-specific
formula or behavioral-state restriction. Generic dispatch selects
`xds_obj$MY_obj[[s]]`. Preserve formulas and flag return-shape or
parameter-lookup discrepancies separately during documentation review.

```{r, eval=TRUE, purl=TRUE}
#' @title Compute infective mosquito biting density for `newMYname` (**MY**)
#' @description Return the daily infective mosquito biting density on humans,
#' `fqZ`, for each patch in the `newMYname` module.
#' @inheritParams ramp.xds::F_fqZ
#' @seealso [F_fqM.newMYname]
#' @return a [numeric] vector of length `nPatches`
#' @export
F_fqZ.newMYname <- function(t, y, xds_obj, s) {
  with(get_MY_vars(y, xds_obj, s), {
    with(xds_obj$MY_obj[[s]], {
      fqZ <- ...
      fqZ
    })
  })
}

#' @title Compute mosquito biting density for `newMYname` (**MY**)
#' @description Return the daily mosquito biting density on humans,
#' `fqM`, for each patch in the `newMYname` module.
#' @inheritParams ramp.xds::F_fqM
#' @seealso [F_fqZ.newMYname]
#' @return a [numeric] vector of length `nPatches`
#' @export
F_fqM.newMYname <- function(t, y, xds_obj, s) {
  with(get_MY_vars(y, xds_obj, s), {
    with(xds_obj$MY_obj[[s]], {
      fqM <- ...
      fqM
    })
  })
}

#' @title Compute egg production for `newMYname` (**MY**)
#' @description Return the number of eggs laid by the adult mosquito population, per patch
#' @inheritSection newMYname Egg Laying
#' @inheritParams ramp.xds::F_eggs
#' @seealso [newMYname], [ramp.xds::EggLaying]
#' @return a [numeric] vector of length `nPatches`
#' @export
F_eggs.newMYname <- function(t, y, xds_obj, s) {
  with(get_MY_vars(y, xds_obj, s), {
    with(xds_obj$MY_obj[[s]], {
      eggs <- ...
      eggs
    })
  })
}
```

## Dynamical parameter accessors

Implement `get_f`, `get_q`, `get_g`, and `get_sigma` methods when the module
supplies those parameters. They return stored realized values, without
evaluating ports or applying effect sizes. Refresh port-backed values through
bionomics and effect-size application first. These accessors are distinct
from the module's documented parameter-reporting convention in `get_MY_pars`.

Use the titles and short descriptions below, inherit the module NULL anchor's
`Parameters` section, and return "a [numeric] vector of length `nPatches`".
The shared generics document dispatch on `xds_obj$MY_obj[[s]]`.
For BQ, BQm, and BRQS, `get_sigma` reads `sigma_b`, the blood-feeding
emigration rate, not `sigma_q`. Their `get_g` methods read `g`; BRQS's
state-specific mortality mismatch remains deferred.

Add these parameters and their biological definitions to the module constructor
and NULL anchor when implementing these optional methods.

```{r, eval=TRUE, purl=TRUE}
#' @title Get the feeding rate for `newMYname` (**MY**)
#' @description Return the stored realized feeding rate per patch.
#' @inheritSection newMYname Parameters
#' @inheritParams ramp.xds::get_f
#' @seealso [newMYname]
#' @return a [numeric] vector of length `nPatches`
#' @export
get_f.newMYname <- function(xds_obj, s = 1) {
  xds_obj$MY_obj[[s]]$f
}

#' @title Get the human blood fraction for `newMYname` (**MY**)
#' @description Return the stored realized human blood fraction per patch.
#' @inheritSection newMYname Parameters
#' @inheritParams ramp.xds::get_q
#' @seealso [newMYname]
#' @return a [numeric] vector of length `nPatches`
#' @export
get_q.newMYname <- function(xds_obj, s = 1) {
  xds_obj$MY_obj[[s]]$q
}

#' @title Get the adult mosquito mortality rate for `newMYname` (**MY**)
#' @description Return the stored realized adult mosquito mortality rate per patch.
#' @inheritSection newMYname Parameters
#' @inheritParams ramp.xds::get_g
#' @seealso [newMYname]
#' @return a [numeric] vector of length `nPatches`
#' @export
get_g.newMYname <- function(xds_obj, s = 1) {
  xds_obj$MY_obj[[s]]$g
}

#' @title Get the patch emigration rate for `newMYname` (**MY**)
#' @description Return the stored realized patch emigration rate per patch.
#' @inheritSection newMYname Parameters
#' @inheritParams ramp.xds::get_sigma
#' @seealso [newMYname]
#' @return a [numeric] vector of length `nPatches`
#' @export
get_sigma.newMYname <- function(xds_obj, s = 1) {
  xds_obj$MY_obj[[s]]$sigma
}
```

## Mosquito-matrix accessors

Use the shared `ramp.xds::get_Omega(xds_obj, s = 1)` and
`ramp.xds::get_Upsilon(xds_obj, s = 1)` to retrieve the stored mosquito
demographic matrix, $\Omega$, and EIP survival-and-dispersal matrix,
$\Upsilon$, respectively. Do not implement module-specific getter methods.
They read `xds_obj$MY_obj[[s]]$Omega` and `xds_obj$MY_obj[[s]]$Upsilon`
without recomputing matrices or modifying the model object. Each returns
a matrix of dimensions `nPatches` by `nPatches`, or `NULL` if the
corresponding matrix is not stored.

Their titles are "Get the mosquito demographic matrix (**MY**)" and
"Get the EIP survival-and-dispersal matrix (**MY**)". Document storage
and the absence of recomputation in `@note`, and link to the other getter,
the corresponding `ramp.xds::change_Omega` or `ramp.xds::change_Upsilon`
function, and `ramp.xds::xds_info_mosquito_demography`.

## Model object and state variables

Use the constructor title "Make a module object for `module` (**MY**)".
Describe parameter initialization and `options` overrides. The constructor,
parameter getter, and parameter changer each link to the other two in
`@seealso`; describe any differences in their parameter coverage.

`make_MY_obj_newMYname` creates the module-specific list and assigns its class.
`setup_MY_obj.newMYname` attaches it to the full `xds_obj`. Include the
parameters and any model-specific objects needed by the equations. Parameters
that use the shared bionomics or dispersal interfaces should be set up with
the corresponding `ramp.xds` helpers.

```{r, eval=TRUE, purl=TRUE}
#' @title Make a module object for `newMYname` (**MY**)
#' @description Create a `newMYname` module object and initialize its parameters.
#' Inspect parameters with [get_MY_pars.newMYname] and change supported values
#' with [change_MY_pars.newMYname]. Values in `options` override parameter arguments.
#' @seealso [get_MY_pars.newMYname], [change_MY_pars.newMYname]
#' @param nPatches number of patches
#' @param options named values that override defaults
#' @return a list
#' @export
make_MY_obj_newMYname <- function(nPatches, options = list(), p1 = 1) {
  with(options, {
    MY_obj <- list()
    MY_obj$p1 <- checkIt(p1, nPatches)
    MY_obj$nPatches <- nPatches
    class(MY_obj) <- "newMYname"
    MY_obj
  })
}

#' @title Set up the module object for `newMYname` (**MY**)
#' @description Set up a `newMYname` module object for the **MY** component
#' and the \eqn{s^{th}} vector species.
#' + Create the module object with [make_MY_obj_newMYname], passing `nPatches` and `options`.
#' + Set initial values using [ramp.xds::setup_MY_inits], passing `options` to override defaults.
#' + Return the updated **`xds`** model object.
#' @note The module object is stored at `xds_obj$MY_obj[[s]]`.
#' @inheritParams ramp.xds::setup_MY_obj
#' @return an **`xds`** model object
#' @export
setup_MY_obj.newMYname <- function(MYname, xds_obj, options = list(), s = 1) {
  xds_obj$MY_obj[[s]] <- make_MY_obj_newMYname(xds_obj$nPatches, options)
  xds_obj <- setup_MY_inits(xds_obj, options = options, s = s)
  xds_obj
}
```

## Parameters

```{r, eval=TRUE, purl=TRUE}
#' @title Get parameters for `newMYname` (**MY**)
#' @description Return the parameters for the `newMYname` module as a named list.
#' @inheritParams ramp.xds::get_MY_pars
#' @seealso [make_MY_obj_newMYname], [change_MY_pars.newMYname]
#' @return a named [list] of parameter values
#' @export
get_MY_pars.newMYname <- function(xds_obj, s = 1) {
  with(xds_obj$MY_obj[[s]], list(p1 = p1))
}

#' @title Change parameters for `newMYname` (**MY**)
#' @description Change parameter values named in `options` for the `newMYname`
#' module, leaving other values unchanged.
#' This example supports changes to `p1`.
#' Call [ramp.xds::MBionomics] at time zero after changing parameters;
#' do not call [ramp.xds::MEffectSizes].
#' @inheritParams ramp.xds::change_MY_pars
#' @seealso [make_MY_obj_newMYname], [get_MY_pars.newMYname]
#' @return an **`xds`** model object
#' @export
change_MY_pars.newMYname <- function(xds_obj, options = list(), s = 1) {
  if ("p1" %in% names(options)) {
    xds_obj$MY_obj[[s]]$p1 <- checkIt(options$p1, xds_obj$nPatches)
  }
  y <- ramp.xds::get_inits(xds_obj, flatten = TRUE)
  xds_obj <- ramp.xds::MBionomics(0, y, xds_obj, s)
  xds_obj
}
```

Implement `get_MY_pars.newMYname` and `change_MY_pars.newMYname` for the
parameters users should inspect and change.

## Initial values

Use the shared `ramp.xds::get_MY_inits` function to return stored initial
values for the selected vector species; do not implement a module-specific
getter. It returns the `inits` field directly as a named list, preserves an
empty list, and returns `NULL` if the field is absent (as in `trivialMY`).
Getter documentation uses "Get initial values (**MY**)", describes returning
stored values, puts storage in `@note`, and links to setup/change functions.

`make_MY_inits_newMYname` returns a named list containing an initial value for
every state variable. `setup_MY_inits.newMYname` stores those values in the
module object, and `change_MY_inits.newMYname` updates named values after
setup.

Use the constructor title and description below, preserving any
model-specific explanation. Its return description is "a named [list] of
initial values". The constructor, setup method, and change method each
link to the other two in `@seealso`.
Document numeric scalar expansion to `nPatches`, module-specific length
exceptions, input restrictions, and internally constructed accessory values
that cannot be set independently through `options`.
For changers, document supported values and special behavior, put storage
explanations in `@note`, and return "an **`xds`** model object". Check
preservation of unspecified values and other species; report implementation
discrepancies separately during documentation alignment.

Partial updates must read fallback values from the selected module's
`inits` list, not from its parent module object; preserve other species
and any fields not supported by the changer.

```{r, eval=TRUE, purl=TRUE}
#' @title Make initial values for `newMYname` (**MY**)
#' @description Create a named list of initial values for the `newMYname` module.
#' Values in `options` override the defaults.
#' @details Initial values must be numeric scalars or have length `nPatches`.
#' Scalars are expanded to that length.
#' @param nPatches number of patches
#' @param options named values that override defaults
#' @param M initial adult mosquito density
#' @param Y initial infected mosquito density
#' @return a named [list] of initial values
#' @seealso [setup_MY_inits.newMYname], [change_MY_inits.newMYname]
#' @export
make_MY_inits_newMYname <- function(nPatches, options = list(), M = 10, Y = 1) {
  with(options, {
    M <- checkIt(M, nPatches)
    Y <- checkIt(Y, nPatches)
    list(M = M, Y = Y)
  })
}

#' @title Set up initial values for `newMYname` (**MY**)
#' @description Set up initial values for the `newMYname` module using
#' [make_MY_inits_newMYname]. Values in `options` override the defaults.
#' @note Initial values are stored at `xds_obj$MY_obj[[s]]$inits`.
#' @inheritParams ramp.xds::setup_MY_inits
#' @seealso [make_MY_inits_newMYname], [change_MY_inits.newMYname]
#' @return an **`xds`** model object
#' @export
setup_MY_inits.newMYname <- function(xds_obj, options = list(), s = 1) {
  xds_obj$MY_obj[[s]]$inits <-
    make_MY_inits_newMYname(xds_obj$nPatches, options)
  xds_obj
}

#' @title Change initial values for `newMYname` (**MY**)
#' @description Change initial values named in `options` for the `newMYname`
#' module, leaving other values unchanged.
#' @note Stored initial values for this module are at
#' `xds_obj$MY_obj[[s]]$inits`.
#' @inheritParams ramp.xds::change_MY_inits
#' @seealso [make_MY_inits_newMYname], [setup_MY_inits.newMYname]
#' @return an **`xds`** model object
#' @export
change_MY_inits.newMYname <- function(xds_obj, options = list(), s = 1) {
  xds_obj$MY_obj[[s]]$inits[names(options)] <- options
  xds_obj
}
```

## Initial-density accessors

Implement `get_M` and `get_Z` only when the module supports these initial
density queries. They return initial adult and infective mosquito densities,
not current solver states or output trajectories. Use the titles and short
descriptions below, inherit the module NULL anchor's `State Variables`
section, and keep model-specific explanations there rather than repeating
derivations in accessor descriptions. The shared generics document dispatch
on `xds_obj$MY_obj[[s]]`.

The examples assume the module stores initial `M` and `Z` values; adapt the
implementation to the module's actual initial-state representation.

```{r, eval=TRUE, purl=TRUE}
#' @title Get the initial adult mosquito density for `newMYname` (**MY**)
#' @description Return the initial adult mosquito density per patch.
#' @inheritSection newMYname State Variables
#' @inheritParams ramp.xds::get_M
#' @seealso [newMYname], [ramp.xds::get_MY_inits]
#' @return a [numeric] vector of length `nPatches`
#' @export
get_M.newMYname <- function(xds_obj, s = 1) {
  ramp.xds::get_MY_inits(xds_obj, s)$M
}

#' @title Get the initial infective mosquito density for `newMYname` (**MY**)
#' @description Return the initial infective mosquito density per patch.
#' @inheritSection newMYname State Variables
#' @inheritParams ramp.xds::get_Z
#' @seealso [newMYname], [ramp.xds::get_MY_inits]
#' @return a [numeric] vector of length `nPatches`
#' @export
get_Z.newMYname <- function(xds_obj, s = 1) {
  ramp.xds::get_MY_inits(xds_obj, s)$Z
}
```

## State indices


Retrieve stored indices with the shared `ramp.xds::get_MY_ix(xds_obj, s = 1)`;
the species index defaults to 1. Do not implement a module-specific getter.
It returns the `ix` field directly: a named list of variable indices, an
empty list if stored, or `NULL` if absent. Getter documentation uses
"Get variable indices (**MY**)", describes returning stored indices for
the selected vector species, puts storage in `@note`, and links to `setup_MY_ix`.

`setup_MY_ix.newMYname` assigns a contiguous index range to each state
variable. The example follows the SI implementation; add or remove index
ranges to match the model and store them in the named list at
`xds_obj$MY_obj[[s]]$ix`.

Use the title and description below, documenting actual allocation order
and block lengths, including any auxiliary or matrix/cohort blocks.
Put storage and the updated maximum in `@note`. Return the model object,
not the index list; flag legacy storage or return errors separately.

```{r, eval=TRUE, purl=TRUE}
#' @title Set up variable indices for `newMYname` (**MY**)
#' @description Assign consecutive variable indices for the `newMYname` module,
#' starting after `xds_obj$max_ix`, and update the maximum index.
#' Allocate blocks in the order `M_ix`, `Y_ix`.
#' Each block has length `nPatches`.
#' @note Indices are stored at `xds_obj$MY_obj[[s]]$ix`.
#' The maximum index is stored at `xds_obj$max_ix`.
#' @inheritParams ramp.xds::setup_MY_ix
#' @return an **`xds`** model object
#' @importFrom utils tail
#' @export
setup_MY_ix.newMYname <- function(xds_obj, s) {
  with(xds_obj, {
    M_ix <- seq(from = max_ix + 1, length.out = nPatches)
    max_ix <- tail(M_ix, 1)

    Y_ix <- seq(from = max_ix + 1, length.out = nPatches)
    max_ix <- tail(Y_ix, 1)

    xds_obj$max_ix <- max_ix
    xds_obj$MY_obj[[s]]$ix <- list(M_ix = M_ix, Y_ix = Y_ix)
    xds_obj
  })
}
```

## Parsing outputs

After solving, retrieve the saved results with the shared
`ramp.xds::get_MY_orbits(xds_obj, s = 1)`; do not implement a module-specific
orbit getter. Its title is "Get orbits (**MY**)". It returns a list of
module-specific orbits (trajectories) for **MY** for the selected species
from `xds_obj$outputs$orbits$MY[[s]]`, with
`time` added from `xds_obj$outputs$time`. It neither parses outputs nor
modifies the model object. Link its documentation to `parse_MY_orbits`
and `xds_solve`.

`parse_MY_orbits.newMYname` extracts the same state variables from the solver
output matrix. It can also return derived quantities, such as prevalence or
parity, when those quantities are defined for the model.

This method processes trajectories after solving. Document derived quantities
and index storage in its Roxygen block, and use "a [list]" for returns.
It returns results without modifying the model object; the output-processing
pipeline stores them at `xds_obj$outputs$orbits$MY[[s]]`.

```{r, eval=TRUE, purl=TRUE}
#' @title Parse outputs for `newMYname` (**MY**)
#' @description Extract the model state outputs for the `newMYname` module
#' from `outputs` and return them by name in a list.
#' @note Variable indices are stored at `xds_obj$MY_obj[[s]]$ix`.
#' @inheritParams ramp.xds::parse_MY_orbits
#' @return a [list]
#' @export
parse_MY_orbits.newMYname <- function(outputs, xds_obj, s) {
  with(xds_obj$MY_obj[[s]]$ix, {
    M <- outputs[, M_ix]
    Y <- outputs[, Y_ix]
    list(M = M, Y = Y)
  })
}
```

## Checks and skill set

Implement `get_skillset_MY.newMYname` to return the module's capabilities
and limitations as a list when queried. Do not store it on the module object
during setup.
Implement `check_MY.newMYname` for model-specific setup
checks that should run before solving.

```{r, eval=TRUE, purl=TRUE}
#' @title Check `newMYname` (**MY**)
#' @description Return the model unchanged; no checks are implemented in this template.
#' @inheritParams ramp.xds::check_MY
#' @return an **`xds`** model object
#' @export
check_MY.newMYname <- function(xds_obj, s) {
  xds_obj
}

#' @title Get the skill set for `newMYname` (**MY**)
#' @description Return the capabilities and compatibilities of the `newMYname` module as a list.
#' @inheritParams ramp.xds::get_skillset_MY
#' @return the **MY** module skill set, as a list
#' @export
get_skillset_MY.newMYname <- function(xds_obj, s) {
  list(dts=FALSE, delay=FALSE)
}
```

## Optional methods and tests

Implement `steady_state_M.newMYname`, `steady_state_Y.newMYname`, or
`steady_state_MY.newMYname` only when the corresponding steady state is
defined for the model. The MY interface does not define MY-specific plotting
generics; model-specific plots can use the parsed output from
`parse_MY_orbits.newMYname`.

Use "Compute steady states for `module` (**MY**)" for method titles.
Descriptions identify the inputs and supported equation system; return tags
identify the actual type and state names. The M, Y, and MY generics dispatch
on `xds_obj$MY_obj[[s]]`. If the module supports multiple equation systems,
follow the basicM pattern: delegate to a module-specific generic that dispatches
on `xds_obj$xds`. Do not imply this second stage exists for every module.
Keep existing list/numeric-vector differences explicit, preserve formulas,
and return values without storing them on the model object.

Add the module to the appropriate source file in `ramp.library` and write
tests that check the equations and integration with `ramp.xds`. For example,
check that initial values have the expected names and dimensions, that
derivatives or updates preserve state ordering, and that the biting and egg
outputs have one value per patch.

## Plotting

Use the shared `ramp.xds::xds_plot_M`, `ramp.xds::xds_plot_Y`, and
`ramp.xds::xds_plot_Z` helpers when parsed outputs include adult, infected,
and infective mosquito densities. The fraction helpers
`ramp.xds::xds_plot_Y_fracs` and `ramp.xds::xds_plot_Z_fracs` require saved
`y = Y/M` and `z = Z/M`; they do not compute fractions.
These ordinary functions read the selected species' saved orbits through
`ramp.xds::get_MY_orbits` and draw one line per patch. Do not implement
module-specific methods for them.

Plot helpers create a new plot unless `add = TRUE`; corresponding
`ramp.xds::xds_lines_*` helpers add lines to an existing plot.
Pass one color or line type for all patches, or vectors with one value per
patch. The helpers return `invisible(NULL)`.
Use titles such as "Plot infected mosquito density (**MY**)" and
"Add lines for the infective mosquito fraction (**MY**)". Keep required
fields and overlay behavior in `@note`, and link plot and line helpers
reciprocally. Module-specific visualization remains optional.

## Reusable model code

**`ramp.xds`** has a modular design that allows published models to serve as
dynamical components in new models for malaria and other mosquito-transmitted
pathogens, including ordinary and delay differential equation models and
stochastic or deterministic discrete-time models.

The mathematics supporting this framework are described in [Spatial Dynamics
of Malaria Transmission](https://journals.plos.org/ploscompbiol/article?id=10.1371/journal.pcbi.1010684){target="_blank"}.
^[Wu SL, Henry JM, Citron DT, Mbabazi Ssebuliba D, Nakakawa Nsumba J, Sánchez C. HM, et al. (2023) Spatial dynamics of malaria transmission. PLoS Comput Biol 19(6): e1010684. https://doi.org/10.1371/journal.pcbi.1010684]
